scope: Pinned PostgreSQL 18.6/Citus 14.1.0 plus planner-costing-v2, retained same-volume history, declared two-reader HTTP budget and tested backup/restore/lifecycle behavior. This is finite test evidence, not a guarantee for arbitrary workloads or hardware.

archive_cohort.ledger_scope: Original November 1 UTC ledger charges canonical tables/indexes, canonical-topic helpers/indexes, all shared Columnar metadata/sequence and app maintenance journals once. All 10 overlapping cold canonical/helper/internal-table relations have identical physical table/index totals in the final November 2 UTC inventory. The small supplemental sequence/journal measurements were not repeated in that inventory.

current_storage.scope: Current whole database includes new ingestion. WAL is separate. Free-space gains also include cache/test cleanup and must not be attributed solely to compression.

final_declared_http_gate.scope: Fixed cases warmed first; normal ingestion continued; no OS/PostgreSQL cache flush. At 16 observations nearest-rank p95 equals maximum.

full_size_snapshot_metadata.scope: Actual metadata snapshot only; no full-history dump or full-history restore was performed.

operator_state.scope: These are development-machine settings, not upstream defaults or a recommendation to disable production backups. Calendar-month policy, not rolling 30 days.

test_cleanup.scope: Separate from compression savings; concurrent live filesystem activity can affect this observation.

limitations: Five simultaneous fresh reader calls were 321.908–429.023 ms; their 250 ms check remains false. Warm calls were 16.375–46.950 ms.
Unrestricted full-text/native-fallback queries retain the separate bounded 10-second policy; not all arbitrary queries are indexed or sub-250 ms.
First-use metadata traversal still costs CPU; sampled memory and a short two-reader load test do not establish capacity for arbitrary concurrency.
Retaining all history still grows indefinitely; source and replacement coexist during migration and the free-space/WAL reserve remains mandatory.

Actual controlled restore was proved on 4,530 rows, with a separate 63,800-archived-row workload proof earlier; metadata capture on the final 18,094,923-row history does not constitute a restore at that full scale.
